title: Phoenix applications
description: For a Phoenix application: CSRF protection and secure browser headers in the browser pipeline, no user input through raw/1, parameterized Ecto fragments and secrets loaded at runtime; builds on the elixir-mix pack.

rules.instruction: Keep `plug :protect_from_forgery` in the router's `:browser` pipeline, as a new Phoenix project has it, and route every browser form through that pipeline.
rules.verification: task verify checks that a router names `protect_from_forgery`; also check that the routes the change adds for browser forms go through the `:browser` pipeline.

rules.instruction: Keep `plug :put_secure_browser_headers` in the `:browser` pipeline: unless already set, it sends a `content-security-policy` of `base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self';`, a `referrer-policy`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff` and `x-permitted-cross-domain-policies: none`.
rules.verification: task verify checks that a router names `put_secure_browser_headers`; also check the headers of a page of the running application.

rules.instruction: Never pass user input to `raw/1`: Phoenix escapes user input in templates by default, and the security guide forbids this one way around it.
rules.verification: Search the change for `raw(` and check that none of its arguments comes from a user or an outside system.

rules.instruction: Pass outside values into an Ecto query or a `fragment` with the pin operator `^`, so that Ecto parameterizes them into the query instead of writing them into its SQL text.
rules.verification: Review each Ecto query and `fragment` the change adds and check that every value from a user or an outside system is pinned with `^`.

rules.instruction: Load secrets such as `SECRET_KEY_BASE` (generated with `mix phx.gen.secret`) and `DATABASE_URL` from environment variables in `config/runtime.exs`, which reads them at boot. A file that holds a secret written in full stays out of version control.
rules.verification: task verify checks that `config/runtime.exs` reads environment variables with `System.get_env`; also check that no committed config file holds a secret.
